# JAIL-QUESTIONNAIRE

A questionnaire pulls knowledge out of someone who holds it, so the user can
decide or scope work. It goes to **one recipient**, filled in on their own time
or together in a meeting. Adapted from Matt Pocock's `to-questionnaire`
(github.com/mattpocock/skills, MIT) under JAIL evidence rules.

## Lanes
- **DISCOVERY:** client intake before an engagement (Signal Results
  diagnostic, brokerage listing, consulting scope). Reusable: build it once
  per offer, adapt per client.
- **DECISION:** a decision the user can't settle alone; the questionnaire
  collects the missing facts from the one person who has them.

## Step 1: Interview about the send, never the subject
The user can always answer these; the subject is the recipient's job.
- **Look up first.** Facts already in the conversation, files, Project docs or
  connected apps are filled in, never asked. A known fact goes in the
  questionnaire as a **confirm** item ("We have 14 employees on file:
  correct?").
- **Ask the frontier only,** at most 3 multiple-choice questions per round,
  recommended option first and worded so "yes" accepts it, plus a last option
  to add context. New context always earns another round.
  1. **Who receives it?** Role, expertise, relationship to the user.
  2. **What must come back?** The specific facts or decisions the user needs.
  3. **How is it answered?** Async (default) or filled in together; deadline.
- When the request already names the recipient and what's needed, skip the
  interview: state those as assumptions and write the questionnaire.
- Done when you can name the recipient, the list of things that must come
  back, and the deadline.

## Step 2: Write it
- **Gap only:** every question targets something the recipient knows and the
  user needs. Cut anything the user could look up.
- **Order:** most important first (async may get one pass); group under
  themes once there are more than about 6 questions. Async limit: **15
  questions**; more → split into a required first pass and an optional second.
- **One idea per question**, never compound; closed choices where the answer
  set is known, open text where it isn't; units and time periods stated
  ("last 12 months", "$ per month").
- **"Why this matters"** line only where a question could be misread or invite
  a throwaway answer.
- **Never ask for** passwords, account or card numbers, ID numbers, or health
  details; route anything regulated through **jail-quarantine**.
- **Client copies:** plain 9th-grade English, no jargon, clean white page.

## Template
```
# <Title>
Purpose: <the decision or scope this feeds> · From: <user> · To: <recipient>
How your answers will be used: <one line> · Please reply by: <date> (about <n> minutes)

## Context
<One short paragraph a recipient outside the user's head needs to answer well.>

## How to answer
Partial answers and "I don't know" help; flag anything you're unsure of.

## <Theme>
### <Question, one idea>
_Why this matters: <only if needed>_
> <answer here>        (closed: ☐ Option A ☐ Option B ☐ Other: ____)

## Anything else?
What didn't we ask that we should know?
```

## Step 3: Deliver and close the loop
- **Show the full questionnaire in the reply**, every question as written;
  a saved file or artifact is extra, never instead.
- **Format:** a Docs artifact or .docx for clients (fill-in friendly); a
  Markdown file in the workspace for internal use; a reusable form artifact
  only when the same intake will be sent many times.
- **Check before sending:** every item from Step 1's "what must come back"
  maps to at least one question; count ≤ 15 (or split); no compound
  questions; no forbidden data asked. Report the mapping in one line.
- **When answers return:** label each as User-provided (recipient, date),
  list gaps and "I don't know"s, and hand off to the consumer skill.

## JAIL-HANDOFF
```
JAIL-HANDOFF:
  skill: jail-questionnaire
  status: complete | partial | blocked | stop
  assumptions: [..]
  unknowns: [..]
  outputs: [questionnaire, coverage map]
  next: jail-task-contract | jail-decide | jail-prospect | jail-bmc | none
  approval_required: [sending to the recipient]
  tested: n/a
```
`status: partial` while waiting on the recipient; sending is the user's call.

## Gotchas
- **Interviewing the user about the subject.** They sent it because they don't
  know; ask about the send.
- **Asking what you could look up.** Every lookup-able question costs the
  recipient's goodwill.
- **Kitchen-sink intake.** 40 questions get skimmed; the top 15 get answered.
- **Compound questions.** "Revenue and margin by line?" gets half an answer.
